title: Remapping key to shortcut doesn't work

status.label: Clarify the remap direction
status.detail: The report configures F2 to emit Ctrl+Shift+R, but its expected behavior describes Ctrl+Shift+R emitting F2; no comments clarify which direction or current-build failure is intended.

judgment.rationale: The issue says the mapping is F2 to Ctrl+Shift+R, while its expected behavior says typing Ctrl+Shift+R should produce F2, which reverses the stated source and target. The report also says pressing F2 does nothing, so a separate failure may remain. No version, screenshot of the mapping row, or comments establish which behavior was tested.
evidence: The issue body says F2 is remapped to Ctrl+Shift+R.
The expected behavior says pressing the shortcut should produce the single key, which is the reverse direction from the stated mapping.
The body reports no result from either the shortcut or original key and does not specify a PowerToys version.
The issue is open, has no comments, and has no assignee.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask the reporter to confirm the exact source-to-target row, which key they press, and whether F2 still fails on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer.

fix_assessment.rationale: The expected direction conflicts with the configured F2-to-Ctrl+Shift+R mapping, and the report provides no current-build version or exact mapping evidence. Clarify the behavior before treating this as a Keyboard Manager code defect.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says F2 mapped to Ctrl+Shift+R does not work, but the expected behavior describes the inverse mapping direction.
known_information: The issue body identifies F2 as the key being remapped to Ctrl+Shift+R.
The expected behavior says pressing the shortcut should output the single key, which describes Ctrl+Shift+R to F2 instead.
The report includes a manual F2/Insert swap as a comparison but does not state the PowerToys version or show the exact mapping row.
inferences: The expectation may be reversed relative to the configured mapping, but the reported failure when pressing F2 could be a separate issue.
issue_context.analysis: The first discriminating evidence is the exact mapping row and trigger key. A current-build test of F2 as the source distinguishes a direction misunderstanding from a real key-to-shortcut failure.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and verified there are no comments, assignees, or reported PowerToys version.
Compared the stated F2-to-shortcut mapping with the reverse direction described in Expected Behavior.

information_gaps.information: A screenshot of the exact Keyboard Manager remap row showing source and target.
information_gaps.why_needed: The written mapping and expected direction conflict, so the actual configuration must be established.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Open the Keyboard Manager remap table and capture the row showing the source key and target shortcut.

information_gaps.information: Which key is pressed and whether pressing F2 with the stated mapping fails on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates a reversed expectation from a current key-to-shortcut engine failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer, configure F2 to Ctrl+Shift+R, press F2, and report the exact result.

comment.body:
Thanks for the details. The mapping you describe is F2 → Ctrl+Shift+R, which means pressing F2 should send Ctrl+Shift+R; the Expected Behavior section instead describes Ctrl+Shift+R producing F2. Could you please:
1. Share a screenshot of the exact Keyboard Manager row so the source and target are clear.
2. Confirm which key you press when nothing happens.
3. Say whether pressing F2 with this mapping still fails on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer.
This will separate a reversed expectation from a current key-to-shortcut failure.
